atomic_requirement:
1. Purpose & Scope
The HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 160 and Part 164, Subparts A and C) requires safeguarding the
confidentiality, integrity, and availability (CIA) of electronic protected health information
(ePHI). This guide operationalizes the Rule's requirements into standards and implementation
specifications that regulated entities must address.
Core CIA definitions (§164.304):
Confidentiality — data/information is not made available or disclosed to unauthorized persons or
processes.
Integrity — data/information has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner.
Availability — data/information is accessible and usable on demand by an authorized person.

2. Applicability — Regulated Entities
Entity Type
Definition
Covered Healthcare
Provider
Provider of medical/health services or supplies who transmits health info electronically
for a transaction with an HHS-adopted standard
Health Plan
Individual/group plan that provides or pays for medical care (incl. Medicare, Medicaid,
group health plans)
Healthcare
Clearinghouse
Public/private entity that converts health data between standard and non-standard
formats
Business Associate
Person/entity performing functions involving PHI on behalf of a covered entity;
independently liable for its own Security Rule violations
Covered entities and business associates must obtain written satisfactory assurances (Business
Associate Agreements, BAAs) that PHI will be protected; BAAs may impose stricter requirements than
the Rule's minimum.

3. Structure of the Security Rule
Six main sections:

article_title: 1. General Rules — baseline requirements, flexibility of approach
atomic_requirement: 1. General Rules — baseline requirements, flexibility of approach, R/A framework
2. Administrative Safeguards (§164.308)
3. Physical Safeguards (§164.310)
4. Technical Safeguards (§164.312)
5. Organizational Requirements (§164.314)

6. Policies, Procedures & Documentation Requirements (§164.316)
Required (R) vs. Addressable (A) implementation specifications:
Required — must be implemented, no exceptions, like a standard itself.
Addressable — the entity must (i) assess whether the specification is reasonable and appropriate for
its environment, then (ii) either implement it, or document why not and implement an equivalent,
reasonable alternative safeguard. "Addressable" never means optional.
Where a standard has no listed implementation specifications (e.g., Assigned Security Responsibility,
Evaluation), compliance with the standard itself is mandatory.
All decisions/assessments regarding addressable specifications must be documented.

article_title: 5. Administrative Safeguards — Key Activities by Standard
atomic_requirement: 5. Administrative Safeguards — Key Activities by Standard

5.1 Security Management Process (164.308(a)(1)) — Foundational standard: implement
policies/procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations.
Risk Analysis (R): conduct accurate, thorough assessment of risks/vulnerabilities to ePHI CIA (see §9
below).
Risk Management (R): implement sufficient security measures to reduce risk to a
reasonable/appropriate level.
Sanction Policy (R): apply sanctions against workforce members who fail to comply.
Information System Activity Review (R): regularly review audit logs, access reports, security incident
tracking.

5.2 Assigned Security Responsibility (164.308(a)(2)) — Designate one individual as Security
Official with final responsibility for security policies/procedures; document the assignment and job
description.

5.3 Workforce Security (164.308(a)(3)) — Ensure appropriate access, prevent unauthorized access.
Authorization/Supervision (A), Workforce Clearance Procedure (A), Termination Procedures (A, incl.
separate voluntary/involuntary processes).

5.4 Information Access Management (164.308(a)(4))
Isolate Healthcare Clearinghouse Function (R) if part of a larger organization.
Access Authorization (A) and Access Establishment/Modification (A): implement least-privilege,
role-based access policies with separation of duties.

article_title: 5.5 Security Awareness and Training (164.308(a)(5)) — Training pr
atomic_requirement:
5.5 Security Awareness and Training (164.308(a)(5)) — Training program for all workforce
members (including management).
Security Reminders (A), Protection from Malicious Software (A), Log-in Monitoring (A), Password
Management (A).
Includes needs assessment, developing/approving a training strategy, delivery, and periodic
evaluation/updates.

5.6 Security Incident Procedures (164.308(a)(6))
Response and Reporting (R): identify and respond to suspected/known incidents, mitigate harmful
effects, document incidents and outcomes, incorporate post-incident analysis (lessons learned) into
policy updates.

5.7 Contingency Plan (164.308(a)(7)) — Establish policies/procedures for responding to
emergencies (fire, vandalism, system failure, natural disaster) that damage systems containing ePHI.
Data Backup Plan (R), Disaster Recovery Plan (R), Emergency Mode Operation Plan (R).
Testing and Revision Procedure (A), Applications and Data Criticality Analysis (A).
Recommended process: contingency planning policy → business impact/criticality analysis →
identify preventive measures → recovery strategy → backup/DR plan → emergency-mode plan →
periodic testing.

5.8 Evaluation (164.308(a)(8)) — Periodic technical/nontechnical evaluation of security measures,
triggered by environmental/operational changes affecting ePHI security, to confirm continued
compliance. Determine internal vs. external evaluator, set standards/measurements, conduct, document
findings, repeat periodically.

article_title: 5.9 Business Associate Contracts and Other Arrangements (164.308(
atomic_requirement:
5.9 Business Associate Contracts and Other Arrangements (164.308(b)(1)) — Written
Contract or Other Arrangement (R): obtain satisfactory assurances (BAAs) that the business associate
will appropriately safeguard ePHI.

article_title: 6. Physical Safeguards — Key Activities by Standard
atomic_requirement: 6. Physical Safeguards — Key Activities by Standard

article_title: 6.1 Facility Access Controls (164.310(a)(1)) — Limit physical acc
atomic_requirement:
6.1 Facility Access Controls (164.310(a)(1)) — Limit physical access to facilities/equipment
housing ePHI while ensuring authorized access.

Contingency Operations (A): access procedures supporting data restoration under the Disaster
Recovery/Emergency Mode plans.
Facility Security Plan (A): safeguard the facility and equipment from unauthorized physical access,
tampering, theft.
Access Control and Validation Procedures (A): control/validate a person's access based on role or
function, incl. visitor control.
Maintenance Records (A): document repairs/modifications to physical security components (locks,
doors, walls).

6.2 Workstation Use (164.310(b)) — (R) Policies/procedures specifying proper functions, manner of
performance, and physical surroundings for workstations that access ePHI.

6.3 Workstation Security (164.310(c)) — (R) Physical safeguards for all workstations accessing
ePHI to restrict access to authorized users (e.g., positioning screens away from public view, physical
locks).

article_title: 6.4 Device and Media Controls (164.310(d)(1)) — Govern receipt/re
atomic_requirement:
6.4 Device and Media Controls (164.310(d)(1)) — Govern receipt/removal of hardware/electronic
media containing ePHI in/out of a facility.
Disposal (R): final disposal of ePHI and/or the hardware/media on which it resides.
Media Re-use (R): remove ePHI before media is made available for reuse.
Accountability (A): maintain a record of hardware/media movements and the responsible person.
Data Backup and Storage (A): create a retrievable, exact copy of ePHI before equipment is moved.

article_title: 7. Technical Safeguards — Key Activities by Standard
atomic_requirement: 7. Technical Safeguards — Key Activities by Standard

7.1 Access Control (164.312(a)(1)) — Technical policies/procedures allowing access only to
authorized persons/software.
Unique User Identification (R): assign a unique name/number to track each user's identity.
Emergency Access Procedure (R): procedures for obtaining necessary ePHI during an emergency.
Automatic Logoff (A): terminate sessions after a period of inactivity.
Encryption and Decryption (A): mechanism to encrypt/decrypt ePHI.

7.2 Audit Controls (164.312(b)) — (R) Hardware, software, and/or procedural mechanisms that
record and examine activity in systems containing/using ePHI.

article_title: 7.3 Integrity (164.312(c)(1)) — Protect ePHI from improper altera
atomic_requirement:
7.3 Integrity (164.312(c)(1)) — Protect ePHI from improper alteration/destruction.
Mechanism to Authenticate ePHI (A): electronic mechanisms to corroborate ePHI has not been
altered/destroyed in an unauthorized manner.

article_title: 7.4 Person or Entity Authentication (164.312(d)) — (R) Verify tha
atomic_requirement:
7.4 Person or Entity Authentication (164.312(d)) — (R) Verify that a person/entity seeking access
to ePHI is who they claim to be.

7.5 Transmission Security (164.312(e)(1)) — Guard against unauthorized access to ePHI
transmitted over a network.

Integrity Controls (A): ensure electronically transmitted ePHI is not improperly modified without
detection.
Encryption (A): encrypt ePHI whenever deemed appropriate.

8. Organizational Requirements — §164.314
Business Associate Contracts (164.314(a)): contracts must require the BA to implement
safeguards, report security incidents, ensure subcontractors agree to the same protections, and
authorize contract termination if the BA violates a material term.
Group Health Plan Requirements (164.314(b)): plan documents must be amended to require
the plan sponsor to reasonably/appropriately safeguard ePHI, ensure adequate separation between
the plan and sponsor, and ensure agents follow the same safeguards.

9. Policies, Procedures & Documentation — §164.316
Policies and Procedures (164.316(a)): (R) implement reasonable/appropriate policies and
procedures to comply with the Rule; policies may be changed at any time provided changes are
documented and implemented per the Documentation standard.
Documentation (164.316(b)): maintain written (may be electronic) records of policies,
procedures, actions, activities, or assessments.
Time Limit (R): retain documentation for 6 years from creation date or last effective date,
whichever is later.
Availability (R): make documentation available to those responsible for implementing the
referenced policies/procedures.
Updates (R): periodically review and update documentation in response to
environmental/operational changes affecting ePHI security.

10. Risk Assessment Methodology (Section 3)
HHS OCR does not mandate a specific methodology; the Rule requires Risk Analysis (R) under
164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A) — an accurate and thorough assessment of potential risks/vulnerabilities to ePHI
CIA. NIST recommends (based on IR 8286A / SP 800-30 / SP 800-37) the following non-sequential
steps:

article_title: 1. Prepare — map where ePHI is created, received, stored, process
atomic_requirement:
1. Prepare — map where ePHI is created, received, stored, processed, transmitted (incl. cloud/third
parties, remote/teleworkers, removable media, IoT medical devices); identify existing controls; scope
covers physical + logical boundaries.

article_title: 2. Identify reasonably anticipated threats — natural, human (inte
atomic_requirement:
2. Identify reasonably anticipated threats — natural, human (intentional/unintentional),
environmental threat sources and events (e.g., phishing, ransomware, insider threat).

article_title: 3. Identify vulnerabilities and predisposing conditions — weaknes
atomic_requirement:
3. Identify vulnerabilities and predisposing conditions — weaknesses a threat could exploit; use
internal (past assessments, pen tests, audits) and external (NVD, vendor data) sources.

article_title: 4. Determine likelihood — rate likelihood of threat occurrence co
atomic_requirement:
4. Determine likelihood — rate likelihood of threat occurrence combined with likelihood of
successfully exploiting a vulnerability (qualitative scale: Very Low → Very High).

article_title: 5. Determine impact — rate the impact to confidentiality, integri
atomic_requirement:
5. Determine impact — rate the impact to confidentiality, integrity, and/or availability if exploited;
consider harm to operations, assets, individuals, other organizations, or the nation.

article_title: 6. Determine risk level — combine likelihood × impact via a risk
atomic_requirement:
6. Determine risk level — combine likelihood × impact via a risk matrix (Low/Moderate/High or a 5-
level scale).

article_title: 7. Document results — record all threat/vulnerability pairs, rati
atomic_requirement:
7. Document results — record all threat/vulnerability pairs, ratings, and overall risk, ideally in a risk
register; share with leadership.
Key terms: threat event, threat source, vulnerability, predisposing condition, likelihood,
impact, risk. Risk assessment is not a one-time task — it must be updated periodically as threats and
the environment change (feeds directly into Risk Management, Section 4).
The HHS Security Risk Assessment (SRA) Tool is a free questionnaire-based aid, mainly for
small/medium entities, but it cannot detect technical vulnerabilities and must be paired with a fuller
methodology (e.g., vulnerability scanning). Using the SRA tool does not by itself equal compliance.

11. Risk Management Guidance (Section 4)
Required under Risk Management (R) — 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(B): implement security measures
sufficient to reduce risks/vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level (164.306(a)).
Risk appetite (enterprise-level guidepost for acceptable risk) vs. risk tolerance (specific, more
granular acceptable-performance-risk threshold within that appetite) — concepts from NIST IR
8286A.
After implementing standards/required/addressable specifications, the entity must re-assess whether
each unacceptable threat/vulnerability pair has been brought within organizational risk tolerance.
If existing Security Rule specifications are insufficient, implement additional security controls
(beyond the Rule's explicit list) to reach tolerance — conduct a cost-benefit analysis; if risk still can't
be reduced cost-effectively, the entity may need to revisit its risk tolerance or redesign the
systems/process handling ePHI.
Document all risk management decisions, rationale, and remediation status (e.g., in the same risk
register used for the risk assessment).

atomic_requirement:
12. Key Definitions (Glossary Highlights — full glossary in
Appendix B of the source)
Term
Definition (§ citation)
Addressable
Implementation specification requiring assessment + either implementation or a
documented, reasonable alternative (§164.306(d)(3))
Administrative
safeguards
Administrative actions/policies/procedures managing selection, development,
implementation, maintenance of security measures + workforce conduct (§164.304)
Business associate
Person/entity performing PHI-related functions/services on behalf of a covered
entity (not a workforce member); independently liable (§160.103)
Covered entity
Health plan, healthcare clearinghouse, or healthcare provider who transmits health
info electronically for a covered transaction (§160.103)
ePHI
Electronic protected health information — PHI transmitted or maintained in
electronic media (§160.103)
Confidentiality /
Integrity / Availability
See Section 1 above (§164.304)
Workforce
Employees, volunteers, trainees, and other persons under the direct control of a
covered entity/business associate
Physical safeguards
Physical measures, policies, procedures protecting electronic information
systems/buildings/equipment from hazards and unauthorized intrusion (§164.304)
Technical safeguards
Technology + policies/procedures for its use that protect ePHI and control access to
it (§164.304)

Condensed from NIST SP 800-66r2 (122 pages) to this ~13-page structured reference for RAG
ingestion. All standards, implementation specifications (R/A), and CFR citations from the original have

been preserved; narrative explanation, worked examples, and footnotes have been condensed.
